title: Injury-report reads as a timestamped series, with the delta published, not the level
rule: Every row is recomputed from the retained capture payloads. The hash in each row is the capture store's own content hash, re-derived from the payload file; a payload that no longer reproduces its published hash fails the verifier.

definitions.surprise: a downgrade (this project's ordering) recorded by a read that is within 24 h of that club's kickoff
definitions.game_status_order: blank < Questionable < Doubtful < Out (ours, not the league's)
definitions.alias: join-only normalisation ARZ→AZ, LAR→LA; payloads keep what each read printed

caveats: The three distinct states span two capture methods (collector read, hand transcription). A state pair whose methods differ is labelled as such: its delta mixes a source change with a method change and cannot be read as pure movement.

Two states with identical cell contents can still carry different content hashes: the hash covers the serialised JSON, including the game_label format, not the facts alone. That is why this builder diffs cells and reports the hash next to it.

The Week 11 report is not in the capture store at all: as of the 2026-11-18 probe the league page still printed Week 10 (data/verification/2026_11_18/). The series is therefore one week deep and the weekly-diff requirement stays PARTIAL until a second week exists.
Kickoff times are the printed ET slots converted with a fixed EST offset (November, no DST change). The Munich fixture's printed slot is a 9:30 AM ET listing.
